condition.note: A speculative-decoding A/B on a DGX Spark (NVIDIA GB10, Linux) with native 0.1.62: llama.cpp v0.9.0 on CUDA. Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 ran with no speculation, MTP and DFlash2; Gemma 4 12B Q4 with none and MTP; Muse Glimmer 30B Q4 with none and DFlash2. Rows marked default use the catalog’s own setting and carry the plain model id. 903 trials, three per arm and scenario, ran November 13–22, 2026, in three rounds with the arm order rotated. Every trial’s engine log confirmed its speculation mode, and none was repeated, replaced or set aside. Speculation changed no measured quality: artifact review means match within 0.1, and no pass-rate difference is significant (Muse with DFlash2 +6.2 points, exact p = 0.055, one of ten tests). Eight failures came from time-based stops that faster decoding might have avoided: 4 for Qwen and 3 for Muse without speculation, 1 for Muse with DFlash2. They count as failures here. Task speeds are engine-log medians over every attempt; speculation decoded 2.7–2.9 times faster. Memory is not shown: the GB10 shares its memory with the GPU in a way the measurement cannot see. Artifact reviews are by Claude Sonnet 5.5, one column per rubric.
condition.design: Three rounds, each running every suite once per arm (count 1), with the arm order rotated per suite and round, so an interrupted sweep still leaves balanced arms. A repetition is a round. Muse Glimmer was added during round 1’s first cell, before any result was read (plan amendment 1).
condition.judging: Each round was judged after it finished. Round 2’s in-driver judge pass exited 0 having judged none of its 301 trials; it was re-run by hand on 2026-11-20 and judged the expected 133. That ledger is the one published.
condition.excludedAttempts: Five verification trials (one tictactoe per original arm, 2026-11-13 07:34–08:07) ran before the sweep to confirm each speculation mode and are not part of this publication.

analysis.method: Paired by scenario: each arm’s mean over its three trials of a scenario, the difference averaged over scenarios, with a 95% bootstrap interval over scenarios (10,000 resamples, seed 20261113) and an exact two-sided sign-flip test over the scenarios whose arms differ. Pass rate covers all 43 scenarios; the review mean covers the 19 scenarios with a rubric. passExSpeed leaves speed-sensitive failures out, which favors the arm that had them, so it bounds rather than estimates.
analysis.multipleTests: Ten tests (five comparisons, two endpoints). With Holm’s correction the smallest p-value would need to be below 0.005.
analysis.speedSensitiveRule: A failure is speed-sensitive when it hit the hard ceiling, or when a stop triggered by elapsed time (the craftbook stale no-write repair loop, or the retry loop’s stall or long path) cut off a model turn that was still running: the daemon logged that turn as stopped within 20 seconds of the harness’s stop. Attempt-counted stops never count, whatever was running.

# Final readout: speculative decoding does not change quality

Ran 2026-11-13 08:07 to 2026-11-22 13:12 on the Spark (GB10), llama.cpp v0.9.0
(native 0.1.62), gezel 9e5fd58f with one dist throughout. Three rounds of the
four scorecard suites (43 scenarios), seven arms, 903 trials, 0 excluded for
running the wrong speculation mode. Each arm launched llama-server with the
same settings (context, f16 KV, one slot, batch, reasoning budget) apart from
the drafter. Judged by claude-sonnet-5-5 on the 19 scenarios with a rubric.
Endpoints are the ones PLAN.md fixed before any trial ran. Full tables:
results.md; interim readouts: ROUND1.md, ROUND2.md.

## Answer

Neither MTP nor DFlash2 changed result quality measurably on any of the three
models. Judge scores match within 0.1 points, and every interval sits inside
the +/-0.5 margin set in advance. No pass-rate difference is significant;
Muse with DFlash2 leans +6 points (exact p=0.055, one of ten tests), with no
mechanism behind it. Matched by scenario, output length and tool calls are the
same. Speculation decodes 2.7-2.9x faster and takes 29-50% less wall time.

## By arm

| Arm | Pass | Judge mean | Decode t/s | Draft acceptance | Median trial (min) | Total h |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qwen none | 120/129 | 6.51 | 12.1 | - | 8.5 | 48.8 |
| qwen mtp | 123/129 | 6.50 | 29.1 | 60.4% | 5.1 | 31.1 |
| qwen dflash | 123/129 | 6.59 | 33.0 | 59.4% | 4.3 | 24.2 |
| gemma none | 103/129 | 4.72 | 28.7 | - | 4.6 | 20.4 |
| gemma mtp | 106/129 | 4.75 | 76.5 | 66.0% | 2.7 | 13.5 |
| muse none | 113/129 | 5.63 | 11.8 | - | 15.6 | 47.9 |
| muse dflash | 121/129 | 5.64 | 34.1 | 59.2% | 6.8 | 33.9 |

## Paired by scenario (A minus B)

95% bootstrap CI over scenarios, plus an exact sign-flip test over the
scenarios whose results differ (the bootstrap is optimistic when only a few
scenarios differ).

| A vs B | Pass diff (pts) | CI | Differ | Exact p | Judge diff | CI | Exact p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qwen mtp vs none | +2.3 | [-3.1, 7.8] | 10 | 0.59 | -0.03 | [-0.25, 0.19] | 0.82 |
| qwen dflash vs none | +2.3 | [-3.1, 8.5] | 9 | 0.62 | +0.06 | [-0.19, 0.32] | 0.67 |
| qwen dflash vs mtp | 0.0 | [-3.1, 3.1] | 4 | 1.00 | +0.09 | [-0.11, 0.27] | 0.39 |
| gemma mtp vs none | +2.3 | [-3.9, 8.5] | 11 | 0.64 | +0.03 | [-0.10, 0.16] | 0.67 |
| muse dflash vs none | +6.2 | [1.6, 11.6] | 8 | 0.055 | +0.02 | [-0.09, 0.13] | 0.79 |

- **Judge.** Equivalent within the +/-0.5 margin for every comparison. The
  round-to-round sign flip (round 1 all toward speculation, round 2 all toward
  `none`) was noise; round 1's qwen dflash +0.40 did not hold.
- **Pass rate.** Nine of ten tests sit far from significance. Muse is the
  exception and does not survive correction for ten tests (Holm needs p < 0.005
  for the smallest). Of Muse `none`'s 16 failures, 3 are speed-sensitive (below)
  against 1 of DFlash2's 8; leaving those out it is +5.0 [0.4, 10.5]. The
  remaining `none` failures are attempt-counted stops (repeat loops, file edits
  that failed five times, retry loops) and three idle chats after the model
  ended its turn. None of them depends on elapsed time, and no product-side
  timer (step-stall pause, one-shot timeout) fired in any Muse `none` trial;
  the two seen in Muse were in DFlash2 trials. Read it as an unexplained lean,
  not an effect.
- **Scenarios moving 2 of 3 or more** go both ways: qwen dflash gains
  author-gate-script and loses export-generalize, gemma mtp gains
  export-generalize and loses ab-test-readout, qwen mtp gains codemod-sweep
  (two of `none`'s failures there were speed-sensitive), muse dflash gains
  route-multi and powerpoint-deck.
- **Output.** On scenarios every trial of both arms passed (26-34 per pair),
  the `none`/speculation ratio of output tokens is 0.97-1.06 (geometric mean)
  and of tool calls 0.97-1.03. Muse `none`'s higher raw median (9.1k vs 7.9k)
  comes from which trials passed.
- **Failure modes** are the same kinds in every arm; there is no crash,
  garbled output, or rollback signature specific to speculation.

## Speed

Speculation triples decode on all three models, with 59-66% of drafted tokens
accepted. On Qwen, DFlash2 decodes 13% faster than MTP (33.0 vs 29.1 t/s) and
used 22% less total wall time with the same pass count. Whole trials speed up
less than decode because prefill and tool time do not change.

## Speed-sensitive stops (a harness effect)

A failure is flagged speed-sensitive when it is a hard ceiling, or a
time-triggered stop that cut off a turn still generating. Eight of 903:
qwen none 4, muse none 3, muse dflash 1, every other arm 0.

Five of the eight are the craftbook `stale no-write repair loop`. Its in-flight
deferral is a flat 4 minutes (`NO_WRITE_REPAIR_INFLIGHT_DEFER_MS` in
evals/src/craftbooks/scenario.ts), not scaled by decode rate as the retry
loop's `shouldDeferRetryLoopForInflight` is, so at about 12 t/s a repair turn
can still be generating when it fires (stopped turns were 242-476 s old). All
five were in `none` arms. Scaling that deferral by throughput would remove the
effect. This was not changed during the run.

## Other findings

- **The judge can fail silently.** Round 2's judge pass exited 0 having judged 0
  of 301. judge-sweep prints "skipped (no artifact)" for any trial the judge
  declines, a failed Claude CLI call included, and discards the judge's log, so
  the cause was not recorded. A re-run the next day judged the expected 133.
  judge-sweep should count failed judge calls separately and exit non-zero when
  it judges none of the eligible trials.
- **The judge covers 19 of 43 scenarios.** A blind pairwise comparison of the
  two arms' outputs on all 43 would test quality where no rubric exists. Not
  built.

## Limits

One machine and one quantization (Q4) per model; three trials per scenario,
so pass-rate resolution is about +/-6 points per comparison. Sampling uses the
catalog's settings (not greedy), so trials differ from one another in every
arm, and a difference smaller than about 6 points would not be visible here.

# Does speculative decoding change quality? (llama.cpp v0.9.0)

Written 2026-11-13, before any trial ran. Owner's question: do DFlash2 or MTP
change result quality, compared with plain one-token-at-a-time decoding?

## Setup

- DGX Spark (GB10, 121 GB unified), linux-arm64 CUDA, native 0.1.62 = llama.cpp
  v0.9.0 b12110 (cd959bae). gezel 9e5fd58f, dist built 2026-11-13 07:04-07:06,
  gilde 0.3.10 (qwen3.8-27b-q4 1.0.7 with the DFlash2 drafter; content floor 1.26317).
- Driver: `run.sh main`. Trials land in `evals/runs/scorecard-spec-ab-2026-11-13-r{1,2,3}/<arm>/<suite>/`.
  Not ingested into the scorecard dataset.

| Arm | Model | Speculation | How it is set |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen3.8-27b-q4.none` | Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 | none | `GEZEL_EVAL_LLAMA_SPEC_TYPE=none` |
| `qwen3.8-27b-q4.mtp` | Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 | MTP, built-in head, n=4 | `GEZEL_EVAL_LLAMA_SPEC_TYPE=draft-mtp` |
| `qwen3.8-27b-q4.dflash` | Qwen 3.8 27B Q4 | DFlash2 drafter, n=4 | catalog default on CUDA |
| `gemma4-12b-q4.none` | Gemma 4 12B Q4 | none | `GEZEL_EVAL_LLAMA_SPEC_TYPE=none` |
| `gemma4-12b-q4.mtp` | Gemma 4 12B Q4 | MTP assistant sidecar, n=4 | catalog default |

Gemma 4 12B has no DFlash drafter in the catalog, so it has two arms.

Suites: core (11), productivity (13), developer (10), complex-work (9) = 43
scenarios. Three rounds; each round runs every suite once per arm (count 1),
with the arm order rotated per suite and round, so a stopped sweep still
leaves balanced arms. 645 trials in total.

## What to expect, and what would break it

llama.cpp verifies a draft by sampling the target model at each drafted
position and keeping drafted tokens only while they equal that sample. The
target's output distribution is therefore unchanged in principle. Differences
can still come from:

1. Batched verification changing floating-point reduction order, which flips
   near-tie tokens. That changes individual outputs, not expected quality.
2. Bugs: KV/recurrent-state rollback after a rejected draft (Qwen 3.8 is hybrid,
   Gemma 4 uses sliding-window attention), draft state saved and restored with
   slots, or the drafter's memory narrowing the context window.
3. Wall-clock effects: the `none` arms decode slower, so any time-based
   watchdog fires more often there. Progress-based terminations are the
   capability signal; a wall-clock termination is a harness artifact.

## Validity check (every trial)

The trial's `daemon.log` must show the arm's speculation: no
`common_speculative_init` and no `draft acceptance` lines for `none`, an MTP
draft context for `mtp`, the DFlash2 drafter for `dflash`. A trial that ran
the wrong mode is excluded and counted in the report.

## Endpoints

Primary, per model, each speculation arm against that model's `none` arm:

1. **Pass rate** (each scenario's own gate). Paired by scenario: the per-scenario
   mean over 3 trials, difference averaged over scenarios, 95% CI from a
   bootstrap over scenarios. Resolution at this n is roughly +/-9 points, so
   "no effect" here means "no effect larger than about 10 points".
2. **Judge mean**, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5` via the Claude CLI) on
   the scenarios with a judge rubric (21 of 43: the anchored games and the
   craftbook scenarios), same pairing and CI. Practical margin +/-0.5.

Secondary: failure modes by arm (progress-based vs wall-clock), trial wall time,
output tokens, decode tokens/s, draft acceptance rate and mean accepted length,
and a scenario-by-scenario table that flags any scenario whose pass count moves
by 2 or more of 3 between arms.

## Verification before round 1 (2026-11-13 07:34-08:07)

- Every trial daemon refused to start until `pnpm deps:install` synced
  `@bendyline/docblocks-cli` 2.7.13 -> 2.7.16 (pin bumped in 6a678408; the
  daemon checks the installed version). Synced at 07:34 after the owner's
  `pnpm all` released the dependency lease. That `pnpm all` also rebuilt
  `packages/core/dist` at 07:30; every verify and main cell uses that build.
- The first Qwen warm topped up the eval cache with the DFlash2 drafter and
  `mmproj-F16.gguf` (the vision encoder, absent from the October cache). One
  attempt failed on a Wi-Fi drop; the next completed at 07:57. All three Qwen
  arms now run with the vision encoder loaded, unlike the October sweep.
- One tictactoe trial per arm, read back from llama-server's own lines:
  qwen none "runs none (Settings)", no draft context; qwen mtp "runs draft-mtp
  (Settings)", MTP draft context on the built-in head; qwen dflash "runs
  draft-dflash (catalog)", loads Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf; gemma none,
  no speculation lines; gemma mtp loads mtp-gemma-4-12B-it-Q4_0.gguf. All five
  passed. Decode: gemma 29.4 t/s none vs 92.5 mtp; qwen 10.9 none vs 36.2 mtp vs
  43.0 dflash. Speculation triples decode on both models here, so the `none`
  arms will take roughly twice the wall-clock of the others (whole trials
  include prefill): estimate about 60 h per round, 7-8 days in all.
- Judge path checked: `eval:judge-sweep` with `GEZEL_JUDGE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5`
  judged all five through the Claude CLI and recorded the model per trial.

## Amendment 1 (2026-11-13, during round 1's first cell, before any main-run result was read)

Owner asked to add Muse Glimmer 30B Q4, the only other catalog model with a
true DFlash2 drafter (same conv/selector design as Qwen's; Gemma 4 12B's only
drafters are first-generation DFlash community GGUFs, and the Nemotron Bolt
drafters are DFlash v1 or the LiLiCorr variant). It has no MTP head, so two arms:

| Arm | Speculation | How it is set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `muse-glimmer-30b-q4.none` | none | `GEZEL_EVAL_LLAMA_SPEC_TYPE=none` |
| `muse-glimmer-30b-q4.dflash` | DFlash2 drafter, n=4 | catalog default on CUDA |

Cached weights and vision encoder match catalog 1.0.4; the harness tops up the
1.65 GB drafter. The driver was paused at a cell boundary and restarted as
`run2.sh` (same cells, plus these two arms in every round and suite; complete
cells skipped; preflight/setup failures retried up to 4 times). New primary
comparison: Muse DFlash2 vs Muse none, same endpoints. Muse's September x3
scorecard without speculation took 60 h, so the run grows by about 4 days.

- Judge: every interval now sits inside the +/-0.5 practical margin. Round 1's
  qwen dflash +0.40 did not repeat.
- Pass: every point estimate but dflash-vs-mtp is positive, by 1-5 points. Muse's
  lower bound touches zero. Of the six scenarios where Muse's two arms differ,
  five favor dflash, and two of those five are `none` failures that were
  speed-sensitive (below). Leaving speed-sensitive stops out, Muse is +4.7
  [-1.2, 11.6] and qwen mtp 0.0.

## Speed confound: now observed

analyze.mjs now flags a failure as speed-sensitive when it is a hard-ceiling
stop, or a time-triggered stop (`stale no-write repair loop`, retry-loop
stall/long path) that cut off a turn still running (daemon.log `EXIT throw ...
stopped before the model finished` within 20 s of the harness terminal).

Rounds 1-2: qwen none 2, muse none 2, muse dflash 1, all others 0.

- r2 qwen none and muse none `craftbook-codemod-sweep`: the stale no-write loop
  fired at 244-246 s while the repair turn was generating. Its in-flight
  deferral is a flat 4 min (`NO_WRITE_REPAIR_INFLIGHT_DEFER_MS`), not scaled by
  decode rate, so an 11-12 t/s turn outlives it. The qwen turn had made six tool
  calls and was in prefill for a write-only repair call when it was stopped.
- r2 muse none `craftbook-edit-midtask` and muse dflash
  `craftbook-export-generalize`: hard ceiling, one in each arm.
- Correction to ROUND1.md: r1 qwen none `craftbook-deep-security-review` was
  flagged too. Its repair turn had ended without the missing section, as
  ROUND1.md says, but the outer session had resumed and was generating (turn
  476 s old) when the stop fired 10 s later. "None was cut off mid-generation"
  holds for the repair turn only.

The flag is conservative: it marks stops that speed could have changed, not
ones it did. Speed-sensitive failures are 4 of 36 failures in the `none` arms
and 1 of 34 in the speculation arms.
